The shop supplies explicit words for success and failure, but its add-to-cart in-progress state has no written state label—the action label remains “Add to cart” while the control becomes disabled. Under the evaluation rule, any success, failure, or in-progress state conveyed by colour/visual change without adjacent wording makes the criterion fail. This shop counterexample is sufficient to falsify the cross-shop/account requirement, although authenticated account flows were not reachable.

The implementation evidence strongly indicates that a changed-price notice does not fade or dismiss itself, so the stated negative anti-pattern is not supported. However, I could not create the prerequisite live price mismatch through the deployed app and therefore could not directly time an actually visible changed-price notice. This is reported as partial rather than resolved to avoid treating an unreachable notice state as a full behavioral observation.

The complete delivered route/page, API-handler, UI-module, library-module, and database-table inventories contain only the brief's requested storefront, checkout, order, downloads, installer, authentication, and account/camera functionality (with generic error and health infrastructure). Direct negative searches found none of the four prohibited module families: staff/admin console, returns/RMA workflow, jobs/careers listing, or legal-document library.

The app's runtime dependency block contains only categories explicitly allowed by the evaluation rule. Direct manifest enumeration and a targeted absence search found no declared client for a second datastore, object store, cache, queue, or third-party mail vendor.

The delivered schema, server computation modules, browser islands, rendering paths, seed data, delivery/protection constants, and billing boundary were checked directly. All app money remains integer minor units until display formatting or the explicitly allowed Kill Bill invoice conversion. Source-wide negative searches found none of the disallowed float/decimal declarations, floating-rate tax computation, fractional minor-unit constants, or parsing from formatted currency strings; the full checkout flow corroborated the integer 10% tax and consistent rendered/confirmed totals.

The requirement says every account-scoped handler must obtain the acting customer through one shared helper. The delivered source instead maintains parallel API-local and server-page acting-customer resolvers, each handling authentication input and calling `customerFromToken`. Although individual handlers generally reuse their stack's resolver and the low-level token decoder is centralized, there is not one shared acting-customer helper across all account-scoped handlers, so the positive criterion is not met.

The catalogue fixtures are centrally owned, but the requirement is conjunctive and requires every fixture insert to add no row on a second run. Catalogue product blocks are fixture rows and are inserted unconditionally without an upsert, conflict clause, existence check, or supporting unique constraint. A second seed run against the same database therefore adds duplicate product-block rows, so R24 is not satisfied.

The criterion is false. Although most listed datastore, SMTP, and payment values are centralized in `src/env.js`, the required payment application credentials are not read under the required environment names, and multiple literal hosts/ports occur outside the configuration module. Either defect is independently disqualifying under the evaluation rule.

The requirement fails because the four labels are not single-owned and shared by every reader/writer. Although the renderer has them in the required order, the seed module spells the labels out again instead of referencing that constant. This is an explicit disqualifier in the evaluation rule, so the criterion is conclusively false regardless of whether a fifth group exists.

Both resolver paths independently inspect authentication input and call `customerFromToken`: grep found `customerFromToken` calls in `src/api/app.js` line 62 and `src/lib/session.js` lines 15 and 19. In particular, `src/lib/session.js` lines 12–14 reads the `authorization` header, recognizes Bearer, and strips the Bearer prefix; `src/api/app.js` has its own authorization/session handling and imports `customerFromToken` directly.

The six API account handlers (`/account/orders`, `/account/orders/:number`, and GET/POST/PATCH/DELETE device routes, `src/api/app.js` lines 249–300) use the API-local `requireCustomer`; source grep found eight `requireCustomer` uses including definitions and handlers.

Server-rendered account handlers use the other resolver from `src/lib/session.js`: account pages pass the resulting `customer.id` into `listDevicesForCustomer`, `deviceForCustomer`, `listOrdersForCustomer`, and `readOrder` in `src/pages/account/cameras/index.astro`, `src/pages/account/cameras/[serial].astro`, `src/pages/account/orders/index.astro`, and `src/pages/account/orders/[number].astro`.

A tree-wide search found two `currentCustomer` definitions (`src/api/app.js` and `src/lib/session.js`), not one shared resolver. evidence: Delivered source `src/lib/schema.js` declares all persisted monetary fields as integer minor units: `variant.price_minor`, `cart_line.unit_price_minor`, order `subtotal_minor`, `shipping_minor`, `tax_minor`, `total_minor`, and order-line `unit_price_minor`/`total_minor` are BIGINT. `src/lib/money.js` is the shared server money implementation. `taxFor(subtotalMinor)` uses integer arithmetic `Math.trunc((Number(subtotalMinor) * 10) / 100)`, and totals are added/subtracted as minor-unit integers. Its division by 100 occurs in `formatUsd`/`minorToDecimalString`, i.e. display and billing-boundary formatting.

Browser island code also retains minor units: `src/islands/CartView.jsx` computes a line display from `line.unit_price_minor * line.quantity`, `PlaceOrder.jsx` submits `expected_total_minor`, and `src/islands/lib.js` formats integer minor units into dollars/cents. The only browser `Number(...)` found outside the formatter was quantity handling in `BuyBox.jsx`, not money.

Server cart/order code carries minor-unit fields throughout: catalogue variants expose `price_minor`; cart lines snapshot `unit_price_minor`; subtotals and line totals are integer multiplication/addition; delivery methods use integer `priceMinor` values (0 and 2500); protection prices are integer minor-unit constants; orders persist minor-unit totals.

Billing is the permitted boundary exception: `src/lib/orders.js` stores `killbill_invoice_amount` via `minorToDecimalString(total)`, while `src/lib/billing.js` converts `amountMinor` to a two-decimal invoice amount immediately before sending it to Kill Bill.

Tree-wide searches found no `parseFloat`, no monetary `parseInt`, no logic parsing/recovering a price/total/amount from `$`-formatted text, no fractional `*Minor` literals, and no monetary float/real/double/decimal schema declarations.

evidence: Direct source inspection found two separate acting-customer resolvers. `src/api/app.js` defines its own `async function currentCustomer(c)` (line 59) and `requireCustomer(c)` (line 80), while `src/lib/session.js` separately exports `async function currentCustomer(request)` (line 11).

Both resolver paths independently inspect authentication input and call `customerFromToken`: grep found `customerFromToken` calls in `src/api/app.js` line 62 and `src/lib/session.js` lines 15 and 19. In particular, `src/lib/session.js` lines 12–14 reads the `authorization` header, recognizes Bearer, and strips the Bearer prefix; `src/api/app.js` has its own authorization/session handling and imports `customerFromToken` directly.

The six API account handlers (`/account/orders`, `/account/orders/:number`, and GET/POST/PATCH/DELETE device routes, `src/api/app.js` lines 249–300) use the API-local `requireCustomer`; source grep found eight `requireCustomer` uses including definitions and handlers.

Server-rendered account handlers use the other resolver from `src/lib/session.js`: account pages pass the resulting `customer.id` into `listDevicesForCustomer`, `deviceForCustomer`, `listOrdersForCustomer`, and `readOrder` in `src/pages/account/cameras/index.astro`, `src/pages/account/cameras/[serial].astro`, `src/pages/account/orders/index.astro`, and `src/pages/account/orders/[number].astro`.

A tree-wide search found two `currentCustomer` definitions (`src/api/app.js` and `src/lib/session.js`), not one shared resolver. A tree-wide `readToken(` search found token decoding centralized in `src/lib/customers.js`, but the acting-customer resolution/header-cookie extraction remains duplicated across the API and page stacks.
verdicts.rationale: The requirement says every account-scoped handler must obtain the acting customer through one shared helper. The delivered source instead maintains parallel API-local and server-page acting-customer resolvers, each handling authentication input and calling `customerFromToken`. Although individual handlers generally reuse their stack's resolver and the low-level token decoder is centralized, there is not one shared acting-customer helper across all account-scoped handlers, so the positive criterion is not met.

evidence: Delivered source `src/lib/seed.js` is the single fixture routine: it imports `CUSTOMERS, PRODUCTS, RELEASES, FIRMWARE, DEVICES, SEED_ORDER` from `./seed-data.js`; a repository search found that `seed-data.js` is imported only by this file.

`src/lib/seed-data.js` contains the pinned fixture sets: two customers; five merchandise catalogue products plus the shipment-protection product/rungs; four Arranger releases; four firmware records; and four devices.

Most fixture inserts in `src/lib/seed.js` are restart-safe: source search found `ON CONFLICT` on customer (line 24), product/handle (34), variant/SKU (42), inventory (49), app release/version (67), firmware/product+build (80), order/number (100), device (126), and ownership (133).

However, each product block is inserted at `src/lib/seed.js:55` with `INSERT INTO product_block (product_id, kind, position, payload)`, and the complete `ON CONFLICT` search for that file shows no conflict clause for this insert. Searches also found no existence check or deletion around the product-block loop.

`src/lib/schema.js:46-51` defines `product_block` with product, kind, position, and payload fields, but searches of the schema's unique constraints/indexes found no unique key for product blocks. Thus the unguarded product-block insert does not even have a uniqueness conflict that could suppress a repeat.

`ensureReady()` only uses an in-memory `migrated` flag (`if (migrated) return` at seed.js:180); a process restart resets that flag and invokes `seed()` again, so it does not make the persistent seed idempotent across runs.
verdicts.rationale: The catalogue fixtures are centrally owned, but the requirement is conjunctive and requires every fixture insert to add no row on a second run. Catalogue product blocks are fixture rows and are inserted unconditionally without an upsert, conflict clause, existence check, or supporting unique constraint. A second seed run against the same database therefore adds duplicate product-block rows, so R24 is not satisfied.

For the remaining named settings, source searches showed `DATABASE_URL`, `PAYMENTS_API_URL`, `PAYMENTS_API_KEY`, `PAYMENTS_API_SECRET`, `SMTP_HOST`, `SMTP_PORT`, `SMTP_USER`, and `SMTP_PASS` are centralized in `src/env.js`; `src/lib/db.js`, `src/lib/mail.js`, and `src/lib/billing.js` import `env` rather than reading those settings directly. Although most listed datastore, SMTP, and payment values are centralized in `src/env.js`, the required payment application credentials are not read under the required environment names, and multiple literal hosts/ports occur outside the configuration module. Either defect is independently disqualifying under the evaluation rule.
